title: Apikolos
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (A Tanna of a baraita.) He is mentioned in Tosefta Chullin, beginning of chapter 8: “Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says: Fowl goes up with cheese on the table. Apikolos says: It is not eaten. Others say: Fowl is eaten.” Hyman considers it clear from this that it is a Tanna’s name. But in Chullin 104b: “Agra, father-in-law of Rabbi Abba, taught: Fowl and cheese are eaten be-apikoren (casually, without being careful with them — Rashi). He taught it and he said it: without washing the hands and without wiping the mouth.” Likewise further on they said: “But Agra taught: Fowl and cheese are eaten be-apikorin, and some say be-apkolis,” and it is explained there to mean a cloth. Hyman infers that they did not have his Tosefta’s reading before them and considers their reading undoubtedly correct.

notes.text: Hyman infers a Tanna from Apikolos in the Tosefta, while presenting the Bavli’s competing word readings. His undoubtedly judgment retains its force and attribution; no new person is admitted from a word alone.

The consulted Chullin 104b directly names Agra and uses apikoren. Hyman’s exact Tosefta reading and the inference that Apikolos is a person remain attributed to him; that Tosefta edition has not been independently inspected here.
